text:
Sara (Customer Ops): Heads up — escalating ticket ACME-12345. Customer on Redwood Private (VPC) reports DNS failures resolving our service endpoint from their app hosts after enabling split-horizon Route53 private hosted zone. They see `curl: (6) Could not resolve host: api.redwood.internal` and `dig` returns NXDOMAIN from the instance resolver. They say public resolution still works from outside their VPC.

Alex (Support Eng): Thanks Sara. Do we have their VPC ID and whether the private hosted zone is in the customer AWS account or a partner account? Also any recent changes to DHCP option sets / resolver rules? :thinking:

Sara (Customer Ops): VPC vpc-0a1b2c3d, zone created in their account as `api.redwood.internal` private hosted zone. They enabled split-horizon so internal should resolve to internal IPs. DHCP options unchanged. Tickets says they attached a Route53 Resolver outbound rule for our public domain to forward to our resolver IPs.

Alex (Support Eng): Ok. Common causes: 1) Private hosted zone not associated with the VPC where app runs; 2) Route53 Resolver rule not associated with the VPC or cross-account rule missing; 3) VPC resolver being bypassed (custom /etc/resolv.conf) or search domain issues. Can you ask customer to run these commands from a failing host and paste output?

Alex (Support Eng): ```
# check which resolver instance is used
cat /etc/resolv.conf
# confirm dig against VPC resolver
dig +short api.redwood.internal @169.254.169.253
# test against public resolver
dig +short api.redwood.internal @8.8.8.8
# traceroute to expected internal IP (if dig returns one)
traceroute -n <internal-ip>
```

Sara (Customer Ops): Pushed commands — customer returned logs: `/etc/resolv.conf` shows `nameserver 172.31.0.2` (VPC resolver). `dig @169.254.169.253 api.redwood.internal` -> NXDOMAIN. `dig @8.8.8.8 api.redwood.internal` -> 3.4.5.6 (public IP).

Jamie (Infra Oncall): That strongly suggests the private hosted zone is either not associated with vpc-0a1b2c3d, or there's an overlapping zone with higher priority returning NXDOMAIN. Sara, can you have them run `aws route53 list-hosted-zones-by-name --dns-name api.redwood.internal` and `aws route53 get-hosted-zone --id <zone-id>` to enumerate VPC associations? If the zone is in another account, they need to create an association request (cross-account) or mirror the zone.

Tom (Eng - Network): Also ask them to check Route53 Resolver rules: `aws route53resolver list-resolver-rules` and `list-resolver-rule-associations` for that VPC. If they intended to forward queries for `api.redwood.internal` to a different resolver, make sure the rule is associated with the VPC. If they're using inbound endpoints for on-prem, ensure security groups allow UDP/TCP 53 from the VPC resolver.

Sara (Customer Ops): They ran `get-hosted-zone` — zone exists but VPC associations list is empty. They created the zone but forgot to associate the VPC where app hosts live. They expected automatic association.

Alex (Support Eng): There you go. For Route53 private hosted zones, association is explicit and per-account. Steps to fix: 1) In the Route53 console or via CLI run `aws route53 associate-vpc-with-hosted-zone --hosted-zone-id Z123 --vpc VPCRegion=us-east-1,VPCId=vpc-0a1b2c3d`. 2) If the zone is in a different AWS account, create an association authorization in the zone owner account and then associate from the target account. See docs: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/Route53/latest/DeveloperGuide/hosted-zones-private-associating-vpc.html

Tom (Eng - Network): Note: If they originally set up split-horizon so the internal name intentionally NXDOMAIN to force public fallback, that could be by design; confirm desired behavior. Also if TLS errors appear after associating (cert mismatch) it's probably because the internal name `api.redwood.internal` is not covered by our public cert. If they need TLS for internal name, options: 1) use the public FQDN internally so cert matches, 2) put an internal load balancer with a cert matching internal CN/SAN, or 3) terminate TLS at customer LB and use mTLS to our endpoint.

Sara (Customer Ops): Customer associated the VPC with the hosted zone and re-tested — `dig @169.254.169.253 api.redwood.internal` now returns `10.10.50.12`. `curl https://api.redwood.internal/health` now connects but returns TLS cert CN mismatch (expected `*.redwood.com`). They're going to switch to internal CNAME `internal-api.redwood.com` that resolves internally to the same IP so cert matches.

Alex (Support Eng): Great. Documenting follow-ups for ticket: - Root cause: private hosted zone existed but was not associated with customer VPC (split-horizon DNS misconfiguration). - Immediate resolution: associate hosted zone with VPC. - Secondary issue: TLS cert CN mismatch when using an internal-only hostname; recommend using a hostname covered by our public cert or deploy matching cert internally. - If cross-account association needed, follow Route53 auth flow.

DeployBot: (automated) ticket ACME-12345 updated: customer-supplied fix applied and verification pending.

Jamie (Infra Oncall): I'll add a short KB note we can paste into support replies: 1) Verify `/etc/resolv.conf` points to VPC resolver, 2) `dig @169.254.169.253 <name>`, 3) ensure Route53 private hosted zone is associated with the VPC(s), 4) check resolver rule associations for forwarding, 5) confirm TLS hostname matches cert. Will attach CLI snippets.

Sara (Customer Ops): Customer confirmed app healthy after changing to `internal-api.redwood.com` — closing on their side. Leaving ticket open for 24h to watch metrics. :thumbsup:

Alex (Support Eng): Thanks all, saving KB to support drive under `support/dns-route53-private-vpc-kb.md`.
